newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures climb on unit outages.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures climb on unit outages.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures climbed in brisk trade Wednesday on news of a host of unexpected generation unit outages in the West, as well as expectations of warm weather in the U.S. Southwest, industry sources said.
"Most of this strength was based on the unit outages," said one Houston-based futures trader.

In the West, Salt River Project (SRP) said its 750 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at its Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Arizona, tripped off line early Tuesday, but was boosting power as of late yesterday.
All three Navajo units had been operating at half load over the past few days due to mild weather and weak demand, SRP said.

Pacific Gas & Electric Co said its Moss Landing natural gas-fired plant in Monterey, Calif., tripped off line late Monday, and was expected to resume operation Wednesday afternoon. The Moss Landing station on the central California coast has two units with a total capacity of 1,500 MW.
The 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico tripped off line Wednesday morning due to a tube rupture, with no information available on a restart.
A new outage was seen at the 700 MW unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired plant in Montana. That unit was expected to return to service early Thursday.

NYMEX July Palo Verde (PV) futures ended up $2.45 at $32.66 following exchanges in a range of $31.20-33.40, while August settled up $1.64 at $33.56 after hitting a new contract high of $34.35 and trade as low as $32.80 per MWh.
July California Oregon Border (COB) closed up 41 cents at $20.10 following exchanges in a range of $20.10-21.25, while August closed up 20 cents at $22.98 after trades at $22.90-24.10 per MWh.
An estimated total of 1,064 COB and 1,381 PV contracts traded.
Physical power prices climbed on the outages, with firm, peak PV electricity for Thursday delivery at $29.00-31.00, compared with $24.00-25.00 for Wednesday delivery.
Firm, peak electricity at COB for Thursday delivery was assessed at $19.00-20.00 per MWh, compared with $15.50-16.50 for Wednesday.

Also impacting western power prices was a Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) committee Tuesday introduction of a proposal to derate the Pacific Intertie transmission system from July 1-30 to 6,300 MW from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
The plan still requires the approval of the WSCC board.
